text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A former corporal with Zimbabwe's once-notorious Fifth Brigade is suing the national army for Z$200,000 in compensation for mental trauma resulting from his participation in the military unit's alleged atrocities in the Matebeleland province during the 1980s.
- The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe has issued two guidelines setting limits on how much banks may lend to individual borrowers, groups of related borrowers and bank insiders.

- The council of Ministers of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) have unanimously agreed to set up an investigations unit to look into alleged administrative problems that now threaten the organisation, sources told The Herald in Lusaka on Thursday night.

- Hundreds of people desperate for government financial aid towards meeting their children's school fees have been spending nights queueing outside social welfare offices since schools opened earlier this week.

- Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe on Thursday urged black farmers to venture into tobacco growing, dairy farming and beef production and said schools should teach students how to grow cash crops because agriculture is the mainstay of the southern African country's economy.
